propositions: The transition command has two distinct force flags with different meanings: --force (bypasses start-work/plan-review gate) and --force-close (bypasses completion-verification/signature gate), while rebar claim uses a single --force flag, causing inconsistency and operator confusion.
The --force-close flag must be renamed to --force on the transition command with explicit rejection (no deprecation alias) so stale callers fail loudly rather than silently continuing to work.

A unified --force[=<reason>] flag should dispatch by target status to bypass either the start-work gate (open -> in_progress) or close gate (-> closed), with --force on close recording (no reason given) as the reason when no value is supplied.

The hand-rolled transition flag parser silently skips unknown tokens, so the retired --force-close spelling requires an explicit rejecting branch that raises CommandError naming --force to prevent silent bypass failures.

Scripts like dependency_audit.py that emit the retired --force-close flag in argv builders must be updated to use the new --force spelling, with regression tests feeding generated argv to the real _parse_flags to catch future emitters of renamed flags.
